title: Initialize and Print a Static Array
description: Declare an integer array named `numbers` of a fixed size of 5. Initialize this array directly during its declaration with the values: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. After initialization, use a loop to print each element along with its index.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Elements are fixed as specified. Use a `for` loop to iterate and print.
sample_output:
Array element at index 0: 10
Array element at index 1: 20
Array element at index 2: 30
Array element at index 3: 40
Array element at index 4: 50

title: Accessing Specific Array Elements
description: Write a C program that declares a character array named `programName` and initialize it with the value "C-Program". Print the first, third, and last character.
constraints: The string 'C-Program' has a fixed length. Correctly identify the index for the last character (remember null termination).
sample_output:
First character: C
Third character: P
Last character: m

title: Calculate Sum of Array Elements from User Input
description: Write a C program that prompts the user to enter 5 integer values. Store these 5 integers into an array. After all inputs are received, calculate the sum of all the elements stored in the array, and print the sum.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Input integers will be between -100 and 100. Use a loop for input and another loop for summation.
sample_output: The sum of all array elements is: 150

title: Find Maximum Element in an Array
description: Develop a C program that reads 5 integer values from the user and stores them in an array. Once the array is populated, your program should traverse the array to find the single largest element and print it.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Input integers will be between -1000 and 1000. Use a loop to find the maximum.
sample_output: The maximum element in the array is: 90

title: Reverse Array Elements In-Place
description: Write a C program that reads 5 integers into an array from the user. After reading, modify the array in-place so that its elements are in reverse order. Print both the original and reversed array, space-separated on one line each.
constraints: Array size is fixed at 5. Input integers will be between 1 and 100. Reverse in-place (no auxiliary array). Print space-separated on one line.

title: Search for an Element in an Array
description: Create a C program that first prompts the user to enter 10 integer values to populate an array. After the array is filled, ask the user to enter a single `search_key` integer. The program should search for this value in the array and print the index (0-based) where it is found. If the element is not found, print 'Element not found'.
constraints: Array size is 10. All integers (array elements and search key) will be between 0 and 100. Implement a linear search.

title: Count Frequency of Each Element in an Array
description: Write a C program that reads 10 integers into an array from the user. Assume that these input integers will be within the range of 1 to 10 (inclusive). Your task is to count how many times each integer (1-10) appears in the array and print the count for each integer that appears at least once.
constraints: Array size is 10. Input elements are guaranteed to be integers between 1 and 10. Use an auxiliary array for counting.
sample_output:
Frequency of elements:
1 appears 3 times
2 appears 3 times
3 appears 2 times
4 appears 1 time
5 appears 1 time

title: Matrix Addition (2x2 Two-Dimensional Arrays)
description: Write a C program that performs matrix addition for two 2x2 integer matrices. Prompt the user to enter the elements for the first matrix row by row, then do the same for the second matrix. After both matrices are filled, sum them and print the resulting matrix.
constraints: Both matrices are fixed 2x2. Matrix elements will be integers between -100 and 100. Use nested loops for input and calculation.

title: Demonstrating Array Out-of-Bounds Access (Undefined Behavior)
description: Write a C program that declares a small integer array, for example, `int arr[5];`. Then, deliberately attempt to write a value to an index that is outside the bounds of this array, e.g., `arr[10] = 99;`. Print a message after the illegal write.
constraints: The array size is small and fixed. The out-of-bounds access should be clearly demonstrable.
sample_output: The program may terminate abnormally with a runtime error such as 'Segmentation fault' or 'Bus error'.

title: Student Exam Score Analysis (2D Array)
description: Imagine you are developing a system to analyze student performance. You have 5 students, and each student has scores for 3 subjects. Represent this as a 2D array. Read all scores from input, then print each student's total score, and then print the average score for each subject.
constraints: Number of students is 5, number of subjects is 3. Scores are integers between 0 and 100. Assume valid numerical input. Use nested loops for input and calculations.
sample_output:
--- Student Totals ---
Student 1 Total: 240
Student 2 Total: 210
Student 3 Total: 270
Student 4 Total: 225
Student 5 Total: 180

--- Subject Averages ---
Subject 1 Average: 71.00
Subject 2 Average: 74.00
Subject 3 Average: 80.00
